messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: P99 latency > 12s for /v1/generate across us-west-2 region. Autoscaling attempted 3x, errors: GPU node ECC errors and thermal warnings. Paging: @Asha (on-call)
Asha: I’m on it, grabbing metrics and logs. Any customer reports so far? @support-sre
support-sre: No direct customer tickets yet, but we’ve seen elevated 500s from a couple of high-traffic tenants. I’ll open a support case if this persists. Sounds like GPU hardware flakiness per the bot.
Diego: Looking at the console — p95 jumped to 1.8s, p99 at ~14s, streaming stalls where tokens stop for 4–8s intermittently. KV cache misses are higher than usual. GPU memory errors in dmesg on node gpu-usw2-19: "GPU ECC error, chip 0".
Marta: Thanks. @Kai can you check node health and whether the node is draining? I can start routing weight off that AZ.
Kai: I’m ssh'ing into the node now. SMM reports thermal throttling events, GPU fan at 100% earlier. NVML shows ECC counts increasing. Running `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL` now.
Kai: (paste) ```
GPU 0
    ECC Errors
        Volatile:  124
    Thermal
        GPU Current Temp : 92 C
        Slowdown Temp    : 88 C
``` 
Kai: That temp is above our safe threshold, likely causing stalls. Node was already flagged for degraded perf by infra-bot.
infra-bot: Node gpu-usw2-19 marked DEGRADED (ECC spikes, thermal) — recommended action: drain + replace GPU. Auto-fallback: redirect requests to dedicated spare pool or fallback CPU instances.
Asha: Initiating emergency mitigation: 1) start draining gpu-usw2-19, 2) increase capacity in spare-gpu-pool by 2 replicas, 3) switch streaming-heavy routes to model-variant-small for 10 minutes. Diego/Marta assist with routing.
Diego: On it. Issuing drain: `kubectl cordon gpu-usw2-19 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data gpu-usw2-19` — pods are rescheduling. Pushing routing change to traffic router: bump fallback weight to 20% and route streaming to model-variant-small.
Marta: Update to canary policy: `if p95 > 2s then route streaming to variant-small for affected tenants`. Deploying policy now.
support-sre: Notifying top 3 affected customers with an incident note: short-term degraded latency and active mitigation. No data loss. ETA for full resolution unknown — will update in 30m.
Asha: Observability check: tracing shows tail stalls occur at token boundary after kv-cache miss + context switch when GPU queues hit error. Looks like ECC event causes intermittent GPU kernel failures that fall back to CPU path, causing multi-second stalls.
Kai: Confirmed. Also NVMe SMART shows increased re-queue related to the node, possibly a broader board issue. I'll open a hardware ticket with the colo and ask for a hot-swap. INFRA: allocate spare host.
Diego: After drain started, p99 dropped to ~6s and p95 to 1.2s within 90s. Token streaming stalls reduced but not gone. Some residual stalls where sessions still on that node are finishing.
Asha: Good progress. Next steps: 1) keep node drained and isolate for forensic logs, 2) schedule immediate hardware replacement, 3) keep traffic policies in place until two consecutive 5m windows meet latency SLOs, 4) run synthetic end-to-end tests for streaming at 75th, 95th, 99th percentiles.
Marta: I'll run the synthetic suite and graph the tail distribution. Sharing results in 10m.
support-sre: Customers acknowledged the notice; they appreciate the proactive update. We got one escalation — enterprise-psi asked for SLA credit if breach holds. Documenting for postmortem.
Asha: Adding incident severity SEV2 due to latency SLO breach and multiple tenants impacted. Logging timeline. Assigning postmortem to Diego + Marta.
Diego: Dumping NVML logs and kernel oops to incident storage: `gsutil cp /var/log/nvidia-nvml.log gs://redwood-incidents/1825000000/` — done.
Kai: Hardware ticket submitted to colo: ticket# COLO-87321 — request expedited swap. Also marking host as DO NOT REUSE until validation.
infra-bot: Spare-gpu-pool scaled +2, drain complete for gpu-usw2-19, pods rescheduled. Healthcheck reports 95% of traffic on healthy nodes now.
Asha: Monitoring for 15 more minutes. If p99 stays <4s and streaming stalls <1% of requests we will lift emergency routing. Keep an eye on ECC counters cluster-wide.
Marta: Synthetic run complete: 95th 1.1s, 99th 3.2s, streaming stall rate 0.6% over last 5m. Graphs: https://console.redwood/synthetic/1825000000 (perm link)
Asha: That's acceptable for now. Support — keep customers updated that hardware swap is scheduled and we'll follow up with root cause and timeline. Diego/Marta — please include kernel/NVML artifacts in the postmortem.
support-sre: Will draft customer follow-up. Also saved incident channel for legal/compliance. Tagging security if needed.
Diego: Noting potential long-term action items: add aggressive preemptive ECC monitoring, auto-drain when temp > 85C or ECC volatile > 50 in 10m. Also consider on-the-fly model-reduction fallback to avoid CPU path when GPU transient failures detected.
Asha: Agreed. For now we mark incident as mitigated but open until hardware replacement and RCA complete. Changing status -> MONITORED.
oncall-bot: Incident 1825000000 status updated: MITIGATED -> MONITORED. Reminder: create postmortem draft within 72h and tag `infra, eng-runtime, eng-ml, support`.
Asha: Thanks team — great coordination. Closing live paging, keep async updates here and in postmortem doc. :thumbsup:"
